samples.summary: Nested shift+click test only compares two paths that now share one resolver
samples.evidence: `it('shift+click paints exactly what the equivalent drag paints')` (nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:206-211) drives a drag, then a shift+click, and asserts the two produce identical rect arrays. After this diff both gestures funnel through the same `resolveCellGesture` (text-editor.ts:2093 and ~2381), so the equality holds by construction even if the shared resolver computes the wrong rectangle for a nested table. The only independent assertion is `expect(dragged.length).toBeGreaterThan(1)`, which is also satisfied by an ordinary multi-line *text* selection highlight — `highlightRects()` (line 171-178) filters purely on `Theme.selectionColor`, which doc-canvas/paint-layout also use for text selection (doc-canvas.ts:478, paint-layout.ts:127). So the test cannot distinguish 'a nested cell rectangle was created' from 'some selection was painted'.

samples.summary: 'covers the merge whole' asserts only a rect count, never geometry
samples.evidence: nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:213-217 asserts `expect(rects).toHaveLength(5)` and nothing else — no positions, widths, or cell read-back. Any five selection-coloured fills pass, including five rects in the wrong columns or a row-1 band only one column wide (exactly the #1049 defect shape). The sibling file table-drag-merge-selection.test.ts builds a calibrated `cellsOf()` read-back (lines ~150-175) that maps rects back to `row,col` addresses; this nested suite, which covers the fix's actual new territory, has no equivalent.

samples.summary: Nested clipboard test asserts row count only, not the copied cells
samples.evidence: The copy test (nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:219-241) asserts `payload.tableCells` is truthy and `toHaveLength(3)` — the row count. It never checks the column count (the merge-expanded range should be 2 columns wide), the identity/content of the copied cells, or that they come from the *inner* table rather than the outer 1x1 one. The fix in `getSelectedTableCells` (text-editor.ts ~4326) resolves a nested table's TableData; a regression that copied the wrong table or the wrong column span would still produce 3 rows and pass.

samples.summary: New cycle guards in findOuterCellAddress and findOutermostTableId are untested
samples.evidence: The diff adds `seen` cycle guards in `findOuterCellAddress` (text-editor.ts:3894-3905) and in the new `findOutermostTableId` (text-editor.ts ~3907-3920), justified by the same 'a cyclic parent chain would hang the tab' argument as the one in `resolveNestedTableLayout`. Only the latter has tests (nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:244-269); nothing constructs a cyclic `blockParentMap` reachable by the two TextEditor helpers, so if either guard is wrong (e.g. `findOutermostTableId` `break`s and then returns a mid-chain id) nothing fails. I grepped the docs test tree for `blockParentMap`, `findOuterCellAddress`, `findOutermostTableId` and reviewed both new test files; only `resolveNestedTableLayout` is exercised with a cyclic map.

samples.summary: resolveCellGesture's cross-table branch and its undefined bail-outs have no nested coverage
samples.evidence: `resolveCellGesture` has a second branch (anchor cell in a different table than the resolved cell) that goes through `findOuterCellAddress` + the outermost table's TableData, plus four new `return undefined` bail-outs (missing `tableData`, missing `targetCell`). The new nested suite only gestures inner-cell → inner-cell; table-drag-merge-selection.test.ts only uses a single top-level table. Nothing drags/shift+clicks from a nested cell out to the enclosing table's cell, and nothing covers the undefined paths, which silently produce no selection (callers fall through to 'clear selection' at text-editor.ts:2114-2118).
searchedFor: read both new test files end to end
grep for nested+outer cross-table gestures in packages/docs/test/view

samples.summary: Cyclic-map tests pass `blocks: []`, so `undefined` is the answer for two possible reasons
samples.evidence: Both walk tests (lines 251-269) call `resolveNestedTableLayout` with `{ blocks: [], blockParentMap }`. With an empty block list the function returns `undefined` at the `lbIdx === -1` check regardless of the cycle guard, so the assertion only really proves 'it terminates' (a missing guard would time out rather than fail an assertion). Including a real top-level layout block would make the tests pin the guard rather than the empty-list path.
